description: This is an interactive map and sortable table of the facilities that fuel America's nuclear power plants, published by the independent site usnuclearpowerplants.com. It tracks 165 facilities across seven stages of the fuel cycle: mining and milling (42), conversion (4), enrichment (15), deconversion (3), fuel fabrication (18), recycling and reprocessing (3) and spent-fuel storage (80). The facilities are shown across all statuses: active 98, standby 12, in development 44 and decommissioned 11. The page also quotes Department of Energy spent fuel inventory to the end of 2024, with 325,787 assemblies and 94,443 metric tons of heavy metal, and US Energy Information Administration uranium purchase figures. Access: free to view in a web browser; no download and no licence are stated on the page. Coverage is the United States. Caveats: the site is not an official register, its facility list and statuses are compiled by the site owner from public sources named only in part, and the update dates were not stated. It suits capacity planning and resilience studies of the nuclear fuel supply chain, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
